hints.title: Consider Concurrency in Growing
hints.text: Planting is strictly sequential, but growing occurs concurrently in the background.

hints.title: Greedy Ordering
hints.text: To minimize the total time, plants that require the longest grow times should be planted as early as possible.

hints.title: Track Cumulative Days
hints.text: Sort the indices by growTime in descending order, then accumulate planting time and track the maximum completion day.

hints.title: Complete Python Solution
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def earliestFullBloom(self, plantTime: List[int], growTime: List[int]) -> int:
        indices = list(range(len(plantTime)))
        indices.sort(key=lambda i: growTime[i], reverse=True)
        curr_day = 0
        max_bloom = 0
        for i in indices:
            curr_day += plantTime[i]
            max_bloom = max(max_bloom, curr_day + growTime[i])
        return max_bloom
```

complexity.time: O(N) single pass or optimal algorithmic traversal
variables: N: input size or row count
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing permutations of planting sequences yields O(N!) factorial runtime.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting indices by descending growTime runs in O(N log N) time and O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize that greedy scheduling by bottleneck grow duration guarantees minimal span.
